blocks.heading: Energy (Tulsa's Primary AI Market)
paragraphs: Tulsa is the home of ONEOK (one of the US's largest natural gas distributors, Tulsa HQ), Williams Companies (pipeline infrastructure, Tulsa HQ), and the broader Oklahoma oil and gas service and exploration industry. ClickMasters builds:

Pipeline operations AI: SCADA data ML for natural gas pipeline anomaly detection, compressor station performance monitoring, and pressure event prediction; integrity assessment AI processing in-line inspection (ILI) data — identifying corrosion, dents, and anomalies requiring investigation; operations optimization ML for ONEOK's and Williams' complex midstream networks.

Oil and gas production AI: Well production optimization ML from production and pressure sensor data; artificial lift optimization (ESP, rod pump) from downhole sensor telemetry; production decline curve analysis and reserve estimation ML.

Renewable energy AI: Wind turbine performance optimization and predictive maintenance for Oklahoma's large wind energy fleet (Oklahoma is a top-5 US wind energy state); solar energy generation forecasting for Oklahoma's growing solar portfolio.

blocks.heading: Aviation MRO (World's Largest Commercial MRO)
paragraphs: American Airlines' Tulsa Maintenance and Engineering Center is the world's largest commercial aircraft maintenance facility — performing heavy MRO on American's fleet. ClickMasters builds:
Computer vision for aircraft structural inspection — detecting corrosion, fatigue cracks, and surface damage on fuselage, wing, and tail structures.
Predictive maintenance for aircraft components — predicting failures from maintenance history, flight cycle data, and sensor readings.
MRO operations analytics — optimizing hangar utilization, parts availability, and labor scheduling for Tulsa's massive MRO operation.

blocks.heading: Healthcare
paragraphs: Ascension St. Francis Health System, Saint Francis Health System, and Oklahoma State University Medical Center. HIPAA-compliant clinical AI for Tulsa's health systems.

sections.title: Tulsa's AI Investment Context
sections.description: Programs and trends shaping Tulsa's AI adoption.

blocks.heading: Tulsa Remote Program
paragraphs: Tulsa's "Tulsa Remote" program — which offered cash incentives for remote workers to relocate to Tulsa — has brought technology talent and AI-competent professionals to the city who are now available to Tulsa's energy, aerospace, and healthcare organizations. The program's success (5,000+ participants over several years) has meaningfully expanded Tulsa's commercial technology capacity.

blocks.heading: Oklahoma's Energy Transition
paragraphs: Oklahoma's energy transition — moving from a pure oil and gas economy toward a mix that includes substantial wind and growing solar — is creating AI investment pressure. Companies that were purely focused on oil and gas production optimization are now building AI for wind turbine operations alongside their traditional petroleum applications. This creates broader AI demand as the same vendors serve Oklahoma's entire energy sector.

blocks.heading: American Airlines' Commitment
paragraphs: American Airlines' commitment to Tulsa as its global MRO hub — representing billions in facility investment — signals confidence in Tulsa's industrial and workforce capabilities that extends to AI adoption. The airline's digital transformation investments in Tulsa's MRO operations are creating demand for AI capabilities that can improve aircraft turnaround time, reduce unscheduled maintenance, and optimize parts availability.
